## Design

### 2026-10-05 — October 5: Learnt the basics of KiCad + Added and wired ESP32, MPU6050, and OLED display in Schematics Editor.

**2h**

October 5: Learnt the basics of KiCad + Added and wired ESP32, MPU6050, and OLED display in Schematics Editor.

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 at 15.33.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/47f68d4907da0df76721e665c8b099c5d56dd9b6ed5266751c7d0c4642a21f37.png)

I had a lot of difficulty having KiCad find the correct libraries so that I could add components and symbols. If anyone is dealing with a similar problem, I would highly recommend this tutorial by  Angus Quigley:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjGqhV3JbKw

Once I had everything set up, I started adding components and symbols, wiring them up as I went along. This is how my schematic looks with the ESP32, OLED display, and MPU6050:

![Screenshot 2026-10-05 at 15.31.32](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/0144594d13baffd9216935cf44869d7b72927665876566959cd76e7a34652d05.png)

I can't wait to see how this turns out!

### 2026-10-07 — **October 6: Brainstormed Starbie's new look!**

**6h**

**October 6: Brainstormed Starbie's new look!**

Following the completion of my schematic of Starbie (following the guide on GitHub), I moved on to trying to assign the components a footprint.

This proved to be quite difficult because KiCad was broken from when I installed, leading to several (simple although tedious) errors that I had to fix. Most of these occured because KiCad was unable to find the correct libraries, often because they were corrupted during download.

After fixing the issues, I finally got into the PCB Editor. I tried moving the components around:

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 20.29.46](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/dd1c6e4b2f8d310b973340180ea3f8422548167b81e5ff33ec8b307c9a2f57be.png)
*(Above) My components in PCB editor*

Moving the components around prompted me to think about how my PCB should look like. The star shape looks cool, but it's not quite me. I spent the next hour brainstorming various shapes and colors (design is important to me), and landed upon these 3 main designs: A shrimp, an eye of providence, and a floppy disk!

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 20.32.15](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/f075805f257d45cc31b54d651aa2f5199336dcd1d100ed497dd1644a388c1467.png)
*(Above) The three final designs*

I decided I liked the floppy disk idea the most, as it leaned into the whole tech part of the project.

Next I set off making some edge cuts in the shape of the floppy disk using a great tutorial on the subject by Psychogenics Technologies.

After I had done this, I tried toying around with copper traces, which proved to be quite hard for me, considering the layout of my components.

![Screenshot 2026-10-06 at 21.52.22](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/395360191e6aa73ce82e814d5b38173018fdb7f759771b89cd18c3604f0865e9.png)
*Routing some traces!*

It was a puzzle, trying to make all the traces limited to the front side (f.cu), and in the end all but 3 traces ended up on the front.The electric work was finished!

At this point I was quite tired, and decided to get some sleep. The next day, I worked on some art for the Floppy. I made this in Canva:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 13.11.53](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/187da81882837e3eefdd1e48e73a174a5f2853650850a6810420dbbc61d6379a.png)
*I made this on Canva :)*

Next, I added this on f.silkscreen:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 11.02.05](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/77118579e4024234031e25bb63bf89c53d472f40f5a5c464704f5b381a64165f.png)

Which eventually led to this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 at 11.03.14](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/wcOBQh83TJiHYcIfFNZDTOPITsdvTWkf/6e5788753f047dc038599fb554f998b86b5e99b11a72f832256db894fe065984.png)

This is what the PCB looks like in 3d Viewer mode. And that's all for today ladies and gentleman! I'll be excited to show you the final Gerber and Drill files (and any other final tweaks).

TL;DR - Added components, brainstormed designs, made edge cuts, routed the PCB with copper wires, and added cosmetic changes on the silkscreen.
